title: 6. Passive Voice & Academic Detachment
group: Module 2 · Band 7.0+ Complex Structures & Range Booster
blocks: The passive across every tense you need, when to choose it, the impersonal “It is …” frames for academic detachment, and the twin pitfalls: wrong participles and overuse.

The passive voice turns the object of an action into the subject of the sentence, so the focus falls on what happens rather than who does it. It is one of the two or three structures that give academic writing its formal, impersonal tone, and it is essential in two specific IELTS places: the Task 1 process diagram, which is written almost entirely in the passive, and the Task 2 essay, where an impersonal register sounds more objective than a personal one. Used well, the passive lifts your tone; used everywhere, it makes writing heavy and evasive.

Compare two sentences that describe the same event: Active: Workers transport the materials. (subject = workers, the doer) / Passive: The materials are transported (by workers). (subject = materials, the receiver)

In the active voice, the subject does the action. In the passive voice, the subject receives the action, and the doer either disappears or is added at the end with by. The formula never changes: Object of the active sentence + a form of be + past participle (+ by + doer). Get the correct form of be (which carries the tense) and the past participle right and the passive is right.
The tense lives in the be part; the past participle stays the same. This table shows the transformation for the tenses you actually need.
Notice the pattern: whatever the tense, you always end with the past participle (transported), and the be form in front of it changes to carry the time.
The passive is a tool for specific situations, not a default. Use it when:
The doer is unknown, obvious, or unimportant. New traffic laws were introduced in 2019. (who introduced them is obvious).
You want an objective, impersonal tone. It is widely believed that education reduces poverty. (more academic than “Many people believe …”)
You are describing a process. First, the raw beans are harvested. They are then dried, roasted, and ground before the coffee is packaged.
6.4 Academic detachment: the impersonal “It is …” structures
A specific, high-value use of the passive is to remove “I” and “people” from a general claim, which sounds more objective. Learn these frames:
People say that tourism harms the coast.
It is said that tourism harms the coast.
Get the past participle right, and do not overuse

The passive needs the third form of the verb, not the base form or the past simple. Bangladeshi learners often drop the participle ending. Irregular past participles must be memorised (see Appendix A): build/built, write/written, take/taken, give/given, show/shown. Also, do not overuse the passive: a whole essay in the passive reads as stiff and can hide who is responsible. In Task 2, mix passive and active.

Pitfall 1 · A missing or wrong past participle.
✗ The materials are transport to the site. / The bridge was build in 1990. / The report was wrote by the committee.
✓ The materials are transported to the site. / The bridge was built in 1990. / The report was written by the committee.

Pitfall 2 · Overusing the passive. The passive belongs mainly in the Task 1 process and in impersonal general claims; your arguments and opinions are usually clearer in the active.
✗ (whole essay in the passive)
✓ (mix passive and active; arguments in the active)

Writing Task 1 process diagrams are the clearest case: because the doer of each step is irrelevant, the whole description runs in the passive present simple. A process answer that stays in the active sounds childish; the passive is expected. Writing Task 2 uses the passive more selectively, for the impersonal tone of general statements. Combined with the active for your own arguments, it shows the examiner you can control register.

Skills: Writing, Speaking
Task 1 process: Once the cocoa pods have been harvested, the beans are removed, fermented, and left to dry in the sun.
Task 2 impersonal: It is often argued that stricter regulation is needed, although the costs are frequently underestimated.
Speaking Part 3: A lot is being done to improve recycling, but more could be achieved with better public awareness.
End of Chapter 6. Chapter 7 (Conditionals, Hedging & Hypothetical Reasoning) follows.

title: 6. Practice · Passive Voice & Academic Detachment
group: Module 2 · Band 7.0+ Complex Structures & Range Booster
blocks: Whatever the tense, the passive always ends in the past participle -- only the 'be' form in front of it changes to carry the time. Learn that one pattern and you can transform any active sentence.
**Why it matters:** The passive appears across every tense, and IELTS Task 1 and academic writing lean on it constantly -- so the transformation needs to be automatic.
The tense lives in the **be** part; the past participle stays the same.
Present simple: Workers transport the goods. → The goods are transported.
Present continuous: Workers are transporting the goods. → The goods are being transported.
Past simple: Workers transported the goods. → The goods were transported.
Notice the constant: whatever the tense, you always end with the past participle (transported), and only the be form in front of it changes to carry the time.

blocks.title: Exercise 6.1 · Active to Passive Transformation
blocks.instructions: Rewrite each active sentence in the passive voice, keeping the same tense. Drop the doer where it is obvious, or keep it with “by” where it adds meaning.

items.prompt: Farmers harvest the crop in October.
items.answer: The crop is harvested in October.
accepted: The crop is harvested in October.
The crop is harvested by farmers in October.

items.prompt: The council will build a new bridge next year.
items.answer: A new bridge will be built next year.
accepted: A new bridge will be built next year.

items.answer: The report was written by the committee.
accepted: The report was written by the committee.

items.prompt: Workers are repairing the road at the moment.
items.answer: The road is being repaired at the moment.
accepted: The road is being repaired at the moment.

items.prompt: People have wasted a great deal of water.
items.answer: A great deal of water has been wasted.
accepted: A great deal of water has been wasted.

items.prompt: The government introduced new laws in 2019.
Someone must clean the equipment after every use.
items.answer: The equipment must be cleaned after every use.
accepted: The equipment must be cleaned after every use.
The raw materials are processed by machines.

items.prompt: They had completed the survey before the deadline.
items.answer: The survey had been completed before the deadline.
accepted: The survey had been completed before the deadline.

items.prompt: Volunteers are planting thousands of trees this year.
items.answer: Thousands of trees are being planted this year.
accepted: Thousands of trees are being planted this year.

items.prompt: The factory produces two thousand cars a day.
items.answer: Two thousand cars are produced a day.
accepted: Two thousand cars are produced a day.

items.prompt: A famous architect designed the building.
items.answer: The building was designed by a famous architect.
accepted: The building was designed by a famous architect.
items.reason: the “by” phrase adds real information, so keep it.

accepted: Recycling should be encouraged by the authorities.

items.prompt: Engineers are testing the new system.
items.answer: The new system is being tested.
accepted: The new system is being tested.

items.prompt: People believe that tourism damages the environment. (use the impersonal “It is …”)
items.answer: It is believed that tourism damages the environment.
accepted: It is believed that tourism damages the environment.

blocks: Recap · Passive Voice for Process Writing

The passive isn't a default -- it's a tool for three specific situations: when the doer is unknown or obvious, when you want an objective tone, and when you're describing a process. Process diagrams are exactly that third case.
**Why it matters:** Process-diagram Task 1s are almost impossible to write naturally without the passive, since the steps matter more than who performs them.
The **doer is unknown, obvious, or unimportant**: New traffic laws were introduced in 2019 (who introduced them is obvious).
You want an **objective, impersonal tone**: It is widely believed that education reduces poverty (more academic than "many people believe").
You are **describing a process** -- a sequence of steps where the focus is the material or product moving through stages, not the people carrying them out.
For process diagrams specifically, keep every step in the passive and in a consistent tense (usually present simple) so the sequence reads as a system, not a story about workers.

blocks.title: Exercise 6.2 · Process Diagram Writing
blocks.instructions: Write one paragraph of about 150 words using the passive present simple throughout and appropriate sequencing words (first, then, next, after that, once, finally).

items.prompt: Write one paragraph of about 150 words describing how glass bottles are recycled, using the passive present simple throughout and sequencing words. Stages: used glass bottles collected from homes and bins; transported to a recycling plant; sorted by colour; washed to remove labels and dirt; crushed into small pieces called cullet; melted in a furnace at very high temperature; moulded into new bottles; new bottles filled, labelled, and sent to shops.
items.answer: The diagram illustrates the process by which used glass bottles are recycled into new ones. First, used bottles are collected from homes and public bins, after which they are transported to a recycling plant. On arrival, the glass is sorted by colour into clear, green, and brown, and it is then washed thoroughly so that labels and dirt are removed. Next, the clean glass is crushed into small fragments known as cullet. Once this stage is complete, the cullet is melted in a furnace at an extremely high temperature until it becomes liquid. The molten glass is then moulded into the shape of new bottles. Finally, the finished bottles are filled, labelled, and sent to shops, where the cycle can begin again.
accepted: The diagram illustrates the process by which used glass bottles are recycled into new ones. First, used bottles are collected from homes and public bins, after which they are transported to a recycling plant. On arrival, the glass is sorted by colour into clear, green, and brown, and it is then washed thoroughly so that labels and dirt are removed. Next, the clean glass is crushed into small fragments known as cullet. Once this stage is complete, the cullet is melted in a furnace at an extremely high temperature until it becomes liquid. The molten glass is then moulded into the shape of new bottles. Finally, the finished bottles are filled, labelled, and sent to shops, where the cycle can begin again.
items.reason: Every step is in the passive present simple (are collected, is sorted, is melted, are sent) because the doer is irrelevant; the sequence is held together by ordering words (first, then, next, once, finally); the tense stays consistent from start to finish.
